statement: If $(x, y)$ is the solution to the system of equations below, what is the value of $x$? $$\begin{aligned} 3x + y &= 17 \\ x - y &= 3 \end{aligned}$$

choices.misconception: I solved the system correctly but gave the value of $y$, which is 2, instead of $x$.
I added the left sides to get $4x$ but subtracted the right sides, so I solved $4x = 14$ and got 3.5.
I found $x = 5$ and $y = 2$ and then gave their sum, 7, instead of $x$.

hints: Notice that the $y$-terms have opposite signs.
Add the two equations so that $y$ cancels, then solve for $x$.

solutions.reliable: Adding the equations: $(3x + y) + (x - y) = 17 + 3$, so $4x = 20$ and $x = 5$. Then $y = x - 3 = 2$. Check: $3(5) + 2 = 17$ and $5 - 2 = 3$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
